A lighthouse $L$ shines a beam that hits the surface of the sea at point $B.$ The light is mounted at a height of $10\,\text{m}$ above the water. As the beam is tilted downward, the angle of elevation $\theta $ made by the beam and the point $B$ is increasing at a rate of $0.12$ radians per second. What is the speed of the light spot as a function of $\theta ?$ 

*Hint*: Remember that speed is always positive or zero.

The speed of the light spot is 
{{field-1}}
$\text{m/s}.$
question.worked_solution:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14212968/assets/bd5afbe33a3a82ec439c5807aa99d1d28639ed74126c2dd483093ca511b253c9.png)

In the figure, $y$ is the height of the lighthouse above the water, and $x$ is the horizontal distance from the lighthouse base to the light spot on the water. The quantity $y=10$ meters does not change with time because the light’s height is fixed.

We wish to calculate $\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}.$ To do this, let's start by setting up a relation between $x$ and $y.$ Relative to the angle $\theta ,$ the sides $x$ and $y$ are the adjacent and opposite, respectively. So, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{tan}⁡\theta  & =\frac{y}{x} \\ \operatorname{tan}⁡\theta  & =\frac{10}{x} \\ x & =\frac{10}{\operatorname{tan}⁡\theta } \\ x & =10\operatorname{cot}⁡\theta .\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we differentiate both sides of the equation with respect to $t$ using implicit differentiation, and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(10\operatorname{cot}⁡\theta ) \\ \frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t} & =(-10{csc}^{2}⁡\theta )\frac{\text{d}\theta }{\text{d}t}.\end{aligned}
$$

From the given information, we have $\frac{\text{d}\theta }{\text{d}t}=0.12.$ Substituting these values into the above, we reach

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t} & =(-10{csc}^{2}⁡\theta )\frac{\text{d}\theta }{\text{d}t} \\ \frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t} & =(-10{csc}^{2}⁡\theta )(0.12) \\ \frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t} & =-1.2{csc}^{2}⁡\theta .\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the speed of the light spot toward the lighthouse is $1.2{csc}^{2}⁡\theta \,\text{m/s}.$
